title: This Bird Flew All the Way Around Antarctica in 46 Days

scenes.text: One albatross flew all the way around Antarctica in forty six days.
Scientists tracked grey headed albatrosses with tiny tags.
These birds can cover six hundred to eleven hundred miles in a single day.
Some circled the whole globe, and a few did it two or three times.
Most of the time, they just glide on the wind over open ocean.
A bird that treats the planet like a racetrack.

description:
A grey-headed albatross flew all the way around Antarctica in just 46 days.
Tracking tags showed that albatrosses can cover 600 to 1,100 miles a day, and some circle the globe two or three times.
How far do you think you could travel in 46 days? Comment below.
first_comment: This albatross flew up to 1,100 miles a day. Where in the world would you fly first?
